### Job Market Analysis with PySpark
Analyzed a 2026 job postings dataset (21 Parquet files) to see how salary and demand vary across the market. I cleaned the data in PySpark, filled missing salaries with medians, and built interactive Plotly charts in a custom pink theme.

**What I found:**

- Project management specialists have the most postings by far, at about 111k.
- Salaries show the widest spread around one year of experience, and the spread narrows as education level rises.
- Full-time roles have the tightest salary ranges, while part-time roles have the lowest.
- Remote roles span the widest range of experience requirements, and onsite roles cluster at 5-10 years.

### California Tech Job Market Analysis
Ran four queries on a job postings dataset to answer practical career questions about pay, remote work, and hiring timing in California's tech industry, then turned each result into a chart with written insights.

**What I found:**

- Median salaries for specialized tech occupations range from about $90k to $255k, with most sitting near $150k.
- ServiceNow leads California companies with 65 remote job postings, well ahead of Western Digital and SanDisk at 40 each.
- Job posting volume stays steady until a mid-year spike in June, then drops to just above baseline.
- Among the metro areas in the data, Washington, DC has the highest average salary, with New York close behind and Dallas much lower.
